headline: Revenue keeps growing but profits sink from year-ago levels
summary_short: Doximity's revenue rose 5.1% year-over-year to $145.4M but net income fell 69.4% y/y to $19.1M and diluted EPS dropped to $0.10 from $0.31, even as full fiscal-year revenue grew 13% to $644.9M.
summary_long: Fiscal Q4 (three months ended March 31, 2026) revenue rose 5.1% y/y to $145.4M but fell 21.4% sequentially; net income dropped 69.4% y/y to $19.1M and diluted EPS to $0.10 from $0.31, with EBITDA down 43.8% y/y to $29.0M. The 10-K's MD&A covers only full fiscal-year results: FY2026 revenue grew 13% to $644.9M on subscription growth (new customers plus 10% higher spend per existing Marketing Solutions customer); R&D rose 40% and sales & marketing 12%, both driven by higher stock-based compensation, holding full-year net margin near 30% versus 39% a year earlier. Cash and marketable securities totaled $748.6M at quarter-end. No numeric forward guidance appears in the filing; Doximity pays no dividend.

drivers.explanation: Management frames FY2026 as continued high-growth-at-scale profitability, citing 13% revenue growth and steady gross margin, while flagging that margins may compress further as it keeps investing in AI initiatives.

FY2026 revenue growth was driven by $64.6M higher subscription revenue: $16.2M from new customers and $48.4M from existing-customer expansion, mainly a 10% rise in average revenue per existing Marketing Solutions customer.
Cost of revenue rose 26% on higher hosting/software costs and amortization tied to AI initiatives and internally-developed software, holding full-year gross margin roughly flat at 89% versus 90%.

Full-year R&D rose 40% and sales & marketing rose 12%, both mostly stock-based-compensation-driven, pressuring operating leverage even as revenue grew; the sharper sequential quarterly decline is not explained in the release.

Full-year net income fell to $196.1M from $223.2M as income tax expense rose 34% (mainly reduced stock-award tax deductions), more than offsetting revenue growth; the quarter-specific decline is not explained in the release.

Cash and cash equivalents rose to $219.2M from $209.6M y/y as $147.2M of investing inflows (security maturities exceeding new purchases and an acquisition payment) offset $464.1M used in financing, mostly $431.7M of share buybacks.
Equity fell as $431.7M of share repurchases retired stock, outweighing the addition of the year's $196.1M net income to retained earnings.
